answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds. Consider a copper as the anchor of the cost.
